We can select a single column by specifying its name in square brackets:[code format="py" codeId="3228"]print(df["ages"]) [/code]

resolved.title: 切片
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Slicing[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Pandas uses the [b]iloc[/b] function to select data based on its numeric index. 
It works the same way indexing lists does in Python.

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="3230"]# third row
print(df.iloc[2])

#first 3 rows
print(df.iloc[:3])

# rows 2 to 3
print(df.iloc[1:3]) [/code]
[note][b]iloc[/b] follows the same rules as slicing does with Python lists.[/note]

[note]Similarly, the or [b]|[/b] operator can be used to combine conditions.[/note]

resolved.title: 等级排名榜
resolved.problem_statement_md:
给定代码包括一个姓名`name`和等级`rank`的DataFrame。

你需要将一个等级作为输入，并从DataFrame中输出相应的**name**列作为**Series**。
resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Ranking Board[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

You are given a DataFrame that includes the [b]names[/b] and [b]ranks[/b] of people. 
You need to take a rank as input and output the corresponding [b]name[/b] column from the DataFrame as a [b]Series[/b].
[note]Note that the rank is an integer, so you need to convert the user input to an integer.[/note]
resolved.hint_md: 注意，等级`rank`是一个整数，所以需要将用户的输入转换为一个整数。

code_templates.solution_code:
import pandas as pd

data = {
   'name': ['James', 'Billy', 'Bob', 'Amy', 'Tom', 'Harry'],
   'rank': [4, 1, 3, 5, 2, 6]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data, index=data['name'])

user_rank = int(input())

print(df["name"][df["rank"]==user_rank])

testcases.expected_output:
Bob    Bob
Name: name, dtype: object
